title: VisuallyHidden
wrapsNative: accessibilityLabel(_:), accessibilityValue(_:), accessibilityHint(_:) and accessibilityHidden(_:) on the element itself
summary: Text for VoiceOver only is set on the element with the accessibility modifiers. There is no hidden view, and Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: To name an icon-only control, to add context that a sighted person gets from the layout ("Save changes to the ticket"), to merge several texts into one spoken phrase, or to hide a decorative image.
whenNotToUse: Do not put a transparent or zero-size Text in the view tree to carry spoken text. Do not hide content that sighted people can see and use.
api: func accessibilityLabel(_ label: String) -> some View
func accessibilityValue(_ value: String) -> some View
func accessibilityHint(_ hint: String) -> some View
func accessibilityHidden(_ hidden: Bool) -> some View
appearance: Nothing is drawn. The modifiers change only what assistive technology reads.
platformNotes: The web hides a span off screen so a screen reader still finds it in the document. iOS has no document: each view is an accessibility element with a label, a value, a hint and traits, so the spoken text is set on the element. A label replaces the visible text for VoiceOver, so start it with the visible words, which Voice Control uses to find the control. Android sets contentDescription and semantics in the same way.
accessibility: accessibilityLabel replaces what VoiceOver reads for the element; accessibilityValue and accessibilityHint are read after it.
accessibilityHidden(true) removes the element and its children from VoiceOver, Switch Control and Voice Control.
accessibilityElement(children: .ignore) with a label makes several views one element with one phrase.
MonarchIcon applies the same rule: without a label it is hidden, with a label it is read.
edgeCases: A label that does not contain the visible text breaks Voice Control's "Tap <name>". Keep the visible words at the start.
accessibilityHidden on a control that can still be tapped leaves it unreachable for VoiceOver users.
Hints may be turned off by the person; do not put essential information in a hint.

examples.title: Extra context, a hidden decoration and two texts read as one
